====== Start a business in New York (LLC filing path) ======

**New York · How do I start a business?** · state model checked by Claude · quality 1.00

//Generated by [[https://github.com/alibama/lexflow|lexflow]] from the state statutes (open-us-law, government publisher text) and checked by Claude: every quoted phrase was matched word for word against the statute text, and the process passed the BPMN/DMN schemas, bpmnlint and a Petri-net soundness check. Information, not legal advice.//

**Governing law:** [[https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/LLC/203|N.Y. LLC Law § 203]] — Formation

  <bpmn:collaboration id="collab_ny_business" name="Start a business in New York (LLC filing path)">
    <bpmn:documentation textFormat="text/plain">Someone wants to start a business, here as a limited liability company</bpmn:documentation>
    <bpmn:extensionElements>
      <lex:model id="ny-business" jurisdiction="ny" jurisdictionName="New York" reviewStatus="draft" method="gold-manual">
        <lex:gap>Only the LLC filing path is modelled step by step. New York issues no certificate of organization: the Department of State only checks that the form is completed and the fee paid, then files and indexes the articles (§ 209), and the LLC is formed on filing or at a later date stated in the articles, up to 60 days (§ 203(d)). The step file_articles stands in for the certificate-and-record steps other states have.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The articles' contents (§ 203(e)) are reduced to the three required items the review can see (name, county, secretary of state as agent for process), the signature (§ 203(a)(ii), § 209) and the fee. Optional items (registered agent, dissolution date, member liability, internal provisions) are not checked. The name rules of LLC Law § 204 and the signing rules of § 207 are not printed here, so who may sign and how is not checked.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Publication (§ 206(a)) is New York's distinctive extra step: the county clerk designates the newspapers, the LLC publishes for six weeks and files proof. Both the six publications and the proof filing must fall within 120 days of formation (the effectiveness of the articles, § 203(d)); the model attaches that limit to both steps, though each timer can only start when its step is reached, not at formation. Missing it suspends the LLC's authority to do business (modelled as right-lapses, ending at authority_suspended). The LLC itself is formed at filing (§ 203(d)); the outcome llc_active marks that publication is proved, so its authority is not subject to suspension. The suspension is lifted whenever proof is filed later, and it does not void contracts or make members liable. Neither is modelled as a path. The publication itself costs whatever the newspapers charge; no statute sets that amount.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Whether the county clerk designates newspapers for each LLC or keeps a standing designation is not said; it is modelled as one step after filing. In counties where no newspaper is designated, newspapers of a neighbouring county may be used (§ 206(a)). Not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The assumed-name filing (Gen. Bus. Law § 130(1)(b)) is placed after publication only because the flow needs one order (a conditional sibling of publication would make the two exclusive); the statute ties it to doing business under another name, not to publication. An LLC trading only under its real name, or with a trade name used together with its real name (§ 130(1-a)(c)), files nothing. The certificate's contents, the 30-day amendment duty (§ 130(3)) and the display duty (§ 130(4)) are cited, not checked step by step. The extra county fees the secretary of state collects for corporations (§ 130(5)(b)(2)) do not apply to LLCs.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Sole proprietors and general partnerships file with the county clerk, not the Department of State (§ 130(1)(a)). The county clerk's fee is in CPLR § 8021(b)(2), which is not printed here. Every general partnership must file a county certificate naming its partners, even under the partners' own names (§ 130(1)(ii)), unless an exemption in § 130(7) applies.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>There is no state business licence in this model. New York has no general state or local business-licence statute like Virginia's BPOL; licences are profession- and activity-specific, and New York City and other localities add their own permits. Sales tax registration and other tax registrations sit in the Tax Law and are not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>A registered limited liability partnership is open only to partnerships of licensed professionals (§ 121-1500(a)(I)). Unlike Virginia, an ordinary general partnership cannot become an LLP. It also publishes within 120 days (§ 121-1500(a)(II)).</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Limited partners' liability shield and its loss through control (Partnership Law § 121-303) are not printed here. The limited partnership row relies on § 121-201 only.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Professionals may face limits on using an ordinary business corporation or LLC instead of a professional entity under the Education Law; not checked here. Design professional service corporations (§ 1503(b-1) to (b-4)) and public accountancy firms (§ 1503(h)) have extra ownership rules not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>A not-for-profit corporation whose purposes need a state official's or agency's consent must obtain it first (N-PCL § 402(a)(2-b), § 404). Not-for-profit status is a state corporate form, not federal tax exemption. Neither is modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Ongoing filings after formation are not modelled: the LLC's statement of address under LLC Law § 301 ($9, § 1101(c)) and a corporation's statement under BCL § 408 ($9, § 104-A(r)); neither section is printed here.</lex:gap>

===== Steps and the words they come from =====

  - **Sign and deliver articles of organization** — Organizer (founder) · //permission// (§ 203(a)) \\ “//(ii) executing such articles of organization in accordance with section two hundred seven of this article and (iii) filing such articles//”
  - **Collect the $200 filing fee** — Department of State (Secretary of State) · //obligation// (§ 1101(f)) \\ “//For filing articles of organization pursuant to section two hundred nine of this chapter, two hundred dollars.//”
  - **Check articles for form and fee** — Department of State (Secretary of State) · //obligation// (§ 209) \\ “//If the instrument that is delivered to the department of state for filing complies as to form with the requirements of law and the filing fee required by any statute of this state in connection therewith has been paid, the instrument shall be filed and indexed by the department of state.//”
  - **File and index the articles** — Department of State (Secretary of State) · //obligation// (§ 209) \\ “//the instrument shall be filed and indexed by the department of state//”
  - **Designate a weekly and a daily newspaper** — County clerk · //obligation// (§ 206(a)) \\ “//in two newspapers of the county in which the office of the limited liability company is located, one newspaper to be printed weekly and one newspaper to be printed daily, to be designated by the county clerk//”
  - **Publish notice weekly for six weeks** — Limited liability company, through a member, manager or authorized person · within 120 days · //obligation// (§ 206(a)) \\ “//a copy of the same or a notice containing the substance thereof shall be published once in each week for six successive weeks//”
  - **File certificate of publication with affidavits** — Limited liability company, through a member, manager or authorized person · within 120 days · //obligation// (§ 206(a)) \\ “//Proof of the publication required by this subdivision, consisting of the certificate of publication of the limited liability company with the affidavits of publication of such newspapers annexed thereto, must be filed with the department of state.//”
  - **Collect the $50 publication filing fee** — Department of State (Secretary of State) · //obligation// (§ 1101(s)) \\ “//For filing a certificate of publication with affidavits of publication annexed thereto pursuant to section two hundred six, eight hundred two, twelve hundred three or thirteen hundred six of this chapter, fifty dollars.//”
  - **File assumed name certificate with Secretary** — Limited liability company, through a member, manager or authorized person · //obligation// (§ 130(1)(b)) \\ “//Such person, if a corporation, limited partnership or limited liability company, shall file, together with the fees as set forth in subdivision five of this section, in the office of the secretary of state a certificate setting forth the name or designation under which business is carried on or conducted or transacted//”
  - **Collect the $25 assumed name fee** — Department of State (Secretary of State) · //obligation// (§ 130(5)(b)(1)) \\ “//for the indexing and filing of such certificates, the secretary of state shall receive a fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00)//”
  - **Index the assumed name certificate** — Department of State (Secretary of State) · //obligation// (§ 130(5)(b)(1)) \\ “//The secretary of state shall keep an alphabetical index of all certificates filed pursuant to paragraph (b) of subdivision one of this section//”

===== Which business structure fits, and what must be filed with the state? =====

^ Organized for a nonprofit or charitable purpose ^ Owners render a licensed professional service ^ Number of owners ^ Owners want protection from the business's debts ^ Plans to sell shares to outside investors ^ Some co-owners will be passive investors only ^ → Business structure ^ → What is filed, and where ^ → State filing fee ^ Source ^

| false | true | - | true | - | - | Professional service corporation (Business Corporation Law Article 15) or professional service limited liability company (LLC Law Article 12); a partnership without limited partners whose partners are professionals may instead register as a registered limited liability partnership (Partnership Law § 121-1500). PC: organized by individuals licensed to render the same professional service, with licensing-authority certificates attached for every proposed shareholder, director and officer (BCL § 1503(a)-(b)). PLLC and LLP: members or partners must be professionals, at least one authorized to practise in New York, but every member or partner must be licensed in listed professions such as medicine, dentistry and engineering (LLC Law § 1203(a), Partnership Law § 121-1500(a)(I), (q)); PLLC articles attach licensing-authority certificates for its individual members and managers (LLC Law § 1203(b)) | Certificate of incorporation (PC) or articles of organization (PLLC) delivered to the Department of State, then a certified copy filed with the licensing authority within 30 days (BCL § 1503%%(c)%%, LLC Law § 1203%%(c)%%(1)); an LLP files a registration with the Department of State. ===== What the text leaves open =====

  * Only the LLC filing path is modelled step by step. New York issues no certificate of organization: the Department of State only checks that the form is completed and the fee paid, then files and indexes the articles (§ 209), and the LLC is formed on filing or at a later date stated in the articles, up to 60 days (§ 203(d)). The step file_articles stands in for the certificate-and-record steps other states have.
  * The articles' contents (§ 203(e)) are reduced to the three required items the review can see (name, county, secretary of state as agent for process), the signature (§ 203(a)(ii), § 209) and the fee. Optional items (registered agent, dissolution date, member liability, internal provisions) are not checked. The name rules of LLC Law § 204 and the signing rules of § 207 are not printed here, so who may sign and how is not checked.
  * Publication (§ 206(a)) is New York's distinctive extra step: the county clerk designates the newspapers, the LLC publishes for six weeks and files proof. Both the six publications and the proof filing must fall within 120 days of formation (the effectiveness of the articles, § 203(d)); the model attaches that limit to both steps, though each timer can only start when its step is reached, not at formation. Missing it suspends the LLC's authority to do business (modelled as right-lapses, ending at authority_suspended). The LLC itself is formed at filing (§ 203(d)); the outcome llc_active marks that publication is proved, so its authority is not subject to suspension. The suspension is lifted whenever proof is filed later, and it does not void contracts or make members liable. Neither is modelled as a path. The publication itself costs whatever the newspapers charge; no statute sets that amount.
  * Whether the county clerk designates newspapers for each LLC or keeps a standing designation is not said; it is modelled as one step after filing. In counties where no newspaper is designated, newspapers of a neighbouring county may be used (§ 206(a)). Not modelled.
  * The assumed-name filing (Gen. Bus. Law § 130(1)(b)) is placed after publication only because the flow needs one order (a conditional sibling of publication would make the two exclusive); the statute ties it to doing business under another name, not to publication. An LLC trading only under its real name, or with a trade name used together with its real name (§ 130(1-a)%%(c)%%), files nothing. The certificate's contents, the 30-day amendment duty (§ 130(3)) and the display duty (§ 130(4)) are cited, not checked step by step. The extra county fees the secretary of state collects for corporations (§ 130(5)(b)(2)) do not apply to LLCs.
  * Sole proprietors and general partnerships file with the county clerk, not the Department of State (§ 130(1)(a)). The county clerk's fee is in CPLR § 8021(b)(2), which is not printed here. Every general partnership must file a county certificate naming its partners, even under the partners' own names (§ 130(1)(ii)), unless an exemption in § 130(7) applies.
  * There is no state business licence in this model. New York has no general state or local business-licence statute like Virginia's BPOL; licences are profession- and activity-specific, and New York City and other localities add their own permits. Sales tax registration and other tax registrations sit in the Tax Law and are not modelled.
  * A registered limited liability partnership is open only to partnerships of licensed professionals (§ 121-1500(a)(I)). Unlike Virginia, an ordinary general partnership cannot become an LLP. It also publishes within 120 days (§ 121-1500(a)(II)).
  * Limited partners' liability shield and its loss through control (Partnership Law § 121-303) are not printed here. The limited partnership row relies on § 121-201 only.
  * Professionals may face limits on using an ordinary business corporation or LLC instead of a professional entity under the Education Law; not checked here. Design professional service corporations (§ 1503(b-1) to (b-4)) and public accountancy firms (§ 1503(h)) have extra ownership rules not modelled.
  * A not-for-profit corporation whose purposes need a state official's or agency's consent must obtain it first (N-PCL § 402(a)(2-b), § 404). Not-for-profit status is a state corporate form, not federal tax exemption. Neither is modelled.
  * Ongoing filings after formation are not modelled: the LLC's statement of address under LLC Law § 301 ($9, § 1101%%(c)%%) and a corporation's statement under BCL § 408 ($9, § 104-A%%(r)%%); neither section is printed here.
